catalog_quote: All lexically heavy monosyllables are stressed, and most polysyllabic words exhibit a distinctly stressed syllable as measured by intensity levels. Although not phonemic, stress influences segmental realisations. For example, unstressed /ɔ/ has a tendency to get centralised and/or unrounded, bringing it very close to some realisations of /ɨ/, but always stays [ɔ] in a stressed position, e.g., in a lexical monosyllable: /mɔ³¹ˈtsʰɑ⁵⁵/ ‘sun’ → [mɔ³¹-] ~ [mʚ³¹-] ~ [mʌ³¹-] ~ [mə³¹-] ~ [mɘ³¹-] /ˈmɔ³¹/ ‘old’ → [mɔ³¹] ... /pʰɔ³¹ˈlɑ³³mɔ³³/ ‘Phola woman’ → [pʰɔ³¹ˈlɑ³³mɔ³³] /male speech ... When it comes to grammatical particles, these often lack autonomous stress and become encliticised to the preceding lexical word (Phola is an SOV and head-modifier language, cf. Section 2 below). ... In contrast, stressed, i.e., lexical, monosyllables, never undergo reduction, and nor do tense vowels, even if they appear in enclitic particles

new_statements.rule_in_words: Phola is a tone language (four contrastive lexical tones 55/33/22/31 plus secondary tones on diphthongs). Word stress exists as a non-phonemic intensity prominence: every lexical monosyllable is stressed, and most polysyllabic words carry one distinctly stressed syllable. The source gives no positional rule; in its two transcribed polysyllables (/mɔ³¹ˈtsʰɑ⁵⁵/ 'sun', /pʰɔ³¹ˈlɑ³³mɔ³³/ 'Phola woman') stress falls on the second syllable, after an unstressed prefix-like first syllable. Grammatical particles are normally unstressed enclitics on the preceding lexical word; tone 22 is shorter and correlates with unstressed syllables (fn. 10, p. 61). Unstressed /ɔ/ and /ɑ/ tend to centralise toward [ɘ]/[ɨ], especially in women's speech.
new_statements.exceptions: The verb 'come' /lɑ³³/ is stressed as a main verb and unstressed as a secondary verb; grammatical particles can take stress for emphasis; tense (creaky) vowels never reduce even in unstressed enclitics; attentional deictics such as tʰuː²² are 'always stressed' and follow a pitch reset (p. 88, p. 100). Vowel reduction under lack of stress is partly a genderlectal feature.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level: lexical words vs enclitic grammatical particles; stress judged by intensity in connected and elicited speech; separate §1.4.5 treats phrase-level intonation (downdrift, pitch reset). Variety: Luodie (lɑ³³ɬe³³/lɑ³³ɬu³³) village, Wadie Township, Yuanjiang County, Yunnan.
new_statements.identity_note: The 2022 thesis describes the Phola of Luodie village (natively lɑ³³ɬe³³ / lɑ³³ɬu³³; 23.459 N, 102.285 E), Wadie Township, Yuanjiang County, Yunnan — Phola proper, Glottolog phol1237 / ISO ypg, the same village as Pelkey 2011's Phola datapoint. It mentions Feikai Phola as a neighbouring dialect. It is not Alo Phola (alop1235, Tuguozhai) nor Phala.

tone_statements.quote: Phola features five lexical pitch contrasts: high-level /55/, mid-level /33/, mid-falling /31/, low-rising /23/ and high-falling /52/. Phonation contrasts are also featured on tonemes /55/, /33/ and /31/. The 52 toneme is the most marginal to the system, and historical dialectology strongly suggests that the Phola /23/ toneme is a recent, ongoing split of mid-level /33/ with allotones including [23ʔ], [35ʔ], [44] and [22]. ... Between a /33/ and /55/ tone, however, /23/ shifts to [44]. By contrast, /33+33+55/ > [33-33-55] with no sandhi effects.
tone_statements.summary: Five tonemes (2 level, 3 contour) obligatory on every syllable, plus tense/lax phonation on /55 33 31/; /23/ a recent split of /33/; sandhi rules given; 20+ tone-marked forms; nothing on stress.

sources.note: Examines pathways by which rising tones arise in Ngwi (Loloish); across 11 Ngwi language clusters a new rising tone value developed from a historically *high tone in nine, sometimes with a prevocalic-consonant-conditioned split, sometimes after both voiced and voiceless onsets; argues a high tonal target favours development of a rising contour. Phola (Luodie) tone reflexes from Pelkey 2011 are part of the compared data (Phula/Southeastern Ngwi cluster); what the paper says specifically about Phola's reflexes was not seen.
